description:
We are a multidisciplinary team combining UX/UI design, data analysis, AI/ML, coding, web development, data management, and communication.

 For the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge, we aim to explore NASA data, identify meaningful trends, and transform complex information into clear and engaging digital experiences.
summary:
Milanko lets anyone explore the Earth like a detective and answer one honest question: did this really change, or does it only look like it? 🌍

We turned decades of NASA data (POWER/MERRA-2 climate records, MODIS vegetation and EONET natural events) into easy-to-read case files. Each one tests one variable in one place and gives a clear verdict, Confirmed ✅ or Inconclusive 🤔, along with how much it changed, in which direction, and what the data cannot claim.

A guided lesson takes you from your own guess to the verdict, a 3D globe lets you explore regions and natural events, and interactive labs show how noise and chance can fool us.

Why it matters 💡 Climate claims are everywhere, but they are rarely tested. Milanko helps students, teachers and curious citizens tell a real trend from chance, using open NASA data, in English and Spanish.
details:
🗂️ Google Drive folder (proposal document, demo video and slides): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RR7d-PP4jFbmrLF71d9NIBAKCB0Ku9nE


🕵️ WHAT IT DOES
Milanko turns an everyday question about the Earth ("Is it hotter here than before?") into an investigation anyone can understand, check and share, using NASA data. Every page answers one question: is this change real, or could it be chance?

📁 Case files: one variable, one place (temperature, rain, vegetation, soil water…). Each shows:
• ⚖️ The verdict: how clear the evidence is (Confirmed or Inconclusive)
• 📈 How much it changed per decade, and which way
• 🚫 What it does NOT say: no predictions, no causes, no advice

❓ "I have a question": pick a topic, what you want to know and a place. A guided lesson walks you through it:
1️⃣ Look at the clues → 2️⃣ Make your own guess → 3️⃣ See the trend line → 4️⃣ Check it with the test → 5️⃣ Read the verdict
📖 Three reading levels (Simple, Guided, Scientific) change the explanation, never the numbers.

🌐 3D globe: spin the Earth, jump to a region, open its case files and see NASA EONET events by year.
🚨 Disaster audit: are there really more disasters, or just more counting? Sometimes the list changed, not the planet.
🧪 Method labs: move the noise and the trend, and watch when the test can (or can't) detect a change.
⚖️ Compare two places · 📥 Download data as CSV · 📋 Copy a citation with its source

⚙️ HOW IT WORKS
• 🛰️ The Milanko API (Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) downloads and stores time series from NASA POWER (MERRA-2), MODIS/Terra (ORNL DAAC) and NASA EONET v3, and exposes them through a documented REST API.
• 📊 Each series is tested with Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope, then published as a case file with its source, method and downloadable data.
• 💻 The portal is built with Next.js, React and TypeScript, with D3 charts and a three.js globe using NASA imagery (Blue Marble, MODIS biomes, ASTER GDEM relief via NASA GIBS). The website is built with Astro.

🎯 BENEFITS & IMPACT
• 🗣️ People hear "it rains more than ever!" every day, but rarely can check it. Now they can, with real NASA data.
• 🎓 It teaches statistical thinking with no science background needed.
• 🤝 "Inconclusive" is treated as an honest answer, not a failure.
• 👩‍🏫 Useful for students, parents helping with homework, teachers, journalists and curious citizens.

🎨 CREATIVITY & DESIGN
• 🕵️ Science as detective work: case files, clues, a hypothesis and a verdict.
• 🧠 We separate "how clear is the evidence" from "how big is the change", because people often mix them up.
• 🌎 Bilingual (English/Spanish) and mobile-friendly
• ♿ Accessible: keyboard navigation, screen readers, reduced motion
• 💬 An optional guided tour on every page

🛠️ TOOLS
Next.js · React · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS · D3 · three.js · Astro · driver.js · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · Docker · GitHub Actions · Vitest · Playwright

🤖 USE OF AI
We used Claude (Anthropic) as a coding assistant to write, review and debug code, and to help write and translate text and prepare the demo materials. Commits made with AI help are marked "Co-Authored-By: Claude" in our Git history. All data and statistical results come from NASA data and our own analysis pipeline, not from AI. This project is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
